# GEO report: ledger-site

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 72/100, Good

Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points).
How it's calculated: low = 16.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 72. High = (16.5 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 72.

The basics are mostly in place: crawlers are allowed in, and the main pages are linked with ordinary links. Four things cost points: no `lang` on `<html>`, no `Sitemap:` line in robots.txt, a Pricing page that is hidden from search but listed in the sitemap, and a Blog that loads its content only in the browser. Nothing is unknown. I read the whole repository (5 routes, the layout and navigation, robots.txt and the sitemap).

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

### 1. Add a language to the page
- **Why it matters:** Search engines and screen readers use `lang` to know what language the site is in.
- **Where:** `app/layout.tsx:11`
- **What the code says:** `<html>`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 18.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 80. The fix is `<html lang="en">`, which matches `site.language` in `geo.config.json`.

### 2. Point robots.txt at your sitemap
- **Why it matters:** Crawlers find the sitemap faster when robots.txt names it.
- **Where:** `public/robots.txt:1`
- **What the code says:** `User-agent: *` (the file has no `Sitemap:` line)
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 18.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 80. Add `Sitemap: https://www.ledger.example/sitemap.xml`.

### 3. Decide whether Pricing should be indexed
- **Why it matters:** Pricing is in the sitemap and has a canonical, but it tells search engines not to index it. Those signals contradict each other.
- **Where:** `app/pricing/page.tsx:1`
- **What the code says:** `robots: { index: false, follow: true }`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** If you remove the noindex, GEO-014 and GEO-015 both clear: 18.25 ÷ 23 × 100 = 79. If the noindex is deliberate, remove Pricing from the sitemap instead. The score then stays at 72, but the contradiction goes away.

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid | Clear | `public/robots.txt`, a few valid lines |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers can get in | Clear | `public/robots.txt:1-2`, `Allow: /`. Only GPTBot (a training crawler) is blocked, which matches your policy |
| GEO-014 | Listed and linked pages are indexable | Problem | `app/pricing/page.tsx:1`, noindex on a sitemap-listed page. 3 of 4 routes clear |
| GEO-015 | Canonical is absolute and indexable | Problem | `app/pricing/page.tsx:1`, canonical points to a noindex page. Home is clear. Docs and Blog have none (see Worth considering) |
| GEO-003 | Content is in server HTML | Problem | `app/blog/page.tsx:8`, `fetch('/api/posts')` inside `useEffect`. 3 of 4 routes clear |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | No JSON-LD found |
| GEO-011 | Sitemap is valid and discoverable | Problem | `public/robots.txt`, no `Sitemap:` line. The sitemap itself is valid |
| GEO-012 | Title, description and html lang | Problem | `app/layout.tsx:11`, `<html>` has no lang. Titles and descriptions are present |
| GEO-016 | Key pages reachable by links | Clear | `app/layout.tsx:13`, plain `<a href>` links to all four pages |
| GEO-017 | Snippets don't block AI search | Clear | `app/layout.tsx:15`, `data-nosnippet` on one element is a deliberate, scoped choice |
| GEO-002 | Accessibility basics | Clear | Read the layout and 5 pages: no images, and links and buttons have text |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app files | Not applicable | No app profile |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt | Not scored | Not present |
| GEO-102 | App structured data | Not scored | Not an app |

## Other problems found

- **Noindex page listed in the sitemap:** `public/sitemap.xml:4`: `<loc>https://www.ledger.example/pricing</loc>`. Pricing is set to noindex, so either remove the noindex or remove the sitemap entry.
- **Blog content depends on an API that isn't in the repo:** `app/blog/page.tsx:8`: `fetch('/api/posts')`. There is no `app/api` folder, so the Blog may show no posts at all. Add the route or load the posts on the server.

## Worth considering

- **Make the Blog render on the server:** `app/blog/page.tsx:1`: `'use client'`. Make it an async server component that fetches the posts. Each post could also get its own page and address, listed in the sitemap.
- **Add canonicals to Docs and Blog:** `app/docs/page.tsx:1`: `metadata = { title: 'Docs', ... }`. Home and Pricing declare canonicals, but these two don't. `metadataBase` in the layout is set, so `alternates: { canonical: '/docs' }` would work.
- **Add Organization and WebSite structured data:** `app/layout.tsx:5`: `title: 'Ledger: accounting for small teams'`. Nothing machine-readable states the site's name and URL. JSON-LD in the layout could do that and might help machines identify the brand.
- **Flesh out Docs:** `app/docs/page.tsx:4`: `Start by importing your bank feed.` The page is a single sentence. Setup steps written as text would answer what a visitor comes for.
- **Spell out Pricing:** `app/pricing/page.tsx:4`: `Free for up to three people.` The description promises "Plans for every team size", but only the free tier appears. Listing the paid plans and prices as text would deliver on that.
- **Give titles more context:** `app/docs/page.tsx:1`: `title: 'Docs'`. "Docs" and "Pricing" don't say whose they are. "Ledger Docs: set up your account" would be clearer.
- **Add `<lastmod>` to the sitemap:** `public/sitemap.xml:3`. Entries have no dates, and `app/sitemap.ts` could generate the file with real ones.
- **Link onward from the home page:** `app/page.tsx:4`: `Invoices, expenses and reports in one place.` The page mentions features but doesn't link to Docs or Pricing in its body.

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs <access log>` to check real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **Live status codes and headers:** a live scan would confirm redirects, `X-Robots-Tag` and that the sitemap URLs answer 200. These are live-only checks and don't change the code results.

## Assumptions

- You want AI search tools to find this site, which matches `policy.aiSearchCrawlers: "allow"`. Blocking GPTBot matches `trainingCrawlers: "block"`.
- I treated the noindex on `/thank-you` as deliberate. It isn't in the sitemap or the navigation, so I left it out of the route counts.
- I treated the noindex on Pricing as probably unintended, since the page is in the sitemap and has a canonical. If it is deliberate, item 3 becomes removing it from the sitemap.
- I read all 5 routes, the layout and navigation, robots.txt, the sitemap and `geo.config.json`. There is no JSON-LD anywhere.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
